items.scope: All Qualys products and vulnerabilities discovered by Qualys that are not covered by another CNA’s scope.

All Wind River branded products as found on windriver.com including vulnerabilities in natively developed or modified product incorporated components, and only product incorporated third-party components not in another CNA’s scope.
WordPress Plugins, Themes, and Core Vulnerabilities discovered by, or reported to, the Wordfence/Defiant team.

Any Seagate or LaCie software or hardware, open or closed source, supported and end of life, as well as any vulnerabilities in third-party software discovered by Seagate that are not in another CNA’s scope.
Adobe issues only.
All Fortra products and vulnerabilities discovered by Fortra in other products not covered by the scope of another CNA.
SailPoint issues only.
M-Files and Hubshare products.
All Proofpoint products.

All products released by Teradyne Robotics subsidiaries, Universal Robots (UR) and Mobile Industrial Robots (MiR), including both actively supported and end-of-life/end-of-service products, as well as vulnerabilities in third-party software identified by Teradyne Robotics that are outside the scope of another CNA.
All HashiCorp products and projects unless covered by another CNA’s scope.
Vulnerabilities in TYPO3 open-source products only, including TYPO3 CMS core and 3rd party extensions for TYPO3, unless covered by the scope of another CNA.
Vulnerabilities discovered in the services and applications of the MeetMe and DuoxMe products that are not covered by another CNA’s scope.
Xpdf open source project, including the xpdf viewer and associated command line tools.
Radiometer products only.
Kubernetes issues only.
All Airbus products (supported products and end-of-life/end-of-service products), as well as vulnerabilities in third-party software discovered by Airbus that are not in another CNA’s scope.
All products and services developed and/or sold by Panasonic Group companies.
Pure Storage products only.
All SAP products.
Third-party products he researches that are not in another CNA’s scope.
Vulnerabilities discovered by or reported to cirosec researchers that are not in another CNA’s scope.

All F5 products and services, commercial and open source, which have not yet reached End of Technical Support (EoTS). All legacy acquisition products and brands including, but not limited to, NGINX, Shape Security, Volterra, and Threat Stack. F5 does not issue CVEs for products which are no longer supported.
All OpenText products (including Carbonite, Zix, Micro Focus, others).
LG Electronics products only.

CVEs requested by code owners using the GitHub Security Advisories feature and vulnerabilities affecting open source projects discovered by security researchers at GitHub or Microsoft not covered by another CNA’s scope.
All Bitdefender products, as well as vulnerabilities in third-party software discovered by Bitdefender that are not in another CNA’s scope.
All Gallagher security products only.
All dotCMS product services including the vulnerabilities reported in our open source core located at https://github.com/dotCMS/core.
All projects listed at https://openjsf.org/projects.
Xerox Corporation issues only.
All Armis products, as well as vulnerabilities in third-party software discovered by Armis that are not in another CNA’s scope.
Intel branded products and technologies and Intel managed open source projects.
Vulnerability assignment related to its vulnerability coordination role.
Vulnerabilities discovered in Extreme Networks, Inc.’s products and services.
Vulnerability assignment related to its vulnerability coordination role.
JetBrains products only.
All ServiceNow products (supported products and end-of-life/end-of-service products), as well as vulnerabilities in third-party software discovered by ServiceNow that are not in another CNA’s scope.
OceanBase products only, not including end-of-life components or products.

All BeyondTrust products, including PasswordSafe, Privileged Remote Access, Remote Support, Privilege Management for Windows/Mac, Privilege Management for Unix/Linux, Identity Security Insights, Active Directory (AD) Bridge, and Total PASM.
Delta Electronics products as listed on www.deltaww.com.

All Cisco products, and any third-party research targets that are not in another CNA’s scope. Cisco will not issue a CVE ID for issues reported on products that are past the Last Day of Support milestone, as defined on Cisco’s End-of-Life Policy, which is available at https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/products/eos-eol-policy.html.
TP-Link issues only.
Juniper issues only.
Qualcomm and Snapdragon issues only.
Switzerland Government Common Vulnerability Program.

Root Scope: European Union (EU) member states/EU authorities, EU CSIRTs network members, and cooperative partners under ENISA’s mandate as well as other CNAs who choose ENISA as their Root.

CNA Scope: Vulnerabilities in information technology (IT) products discovered by European Union (EU) Computer Security Incident Response Teams (CSIRTs) or reported to EU CSIRTs for coordinated disclosure, as long as they do not fall under a CNA with a more specific scope.
All HCL products only.
Vulnerabilities in software discovered by DIVD, and vulnerabilities reported to DIVD for coordinated disclosure, which are not in another CNA’s scope.
Transport Layer Security (TLS) and Cryptographic issues found in wolfSSL products.
